item.text: {"text":"Timestamp-aware attention has relevant precedents, though these do not establish gains on the matched Amazon benchmark. [TiSASRec (2020)](https://jiachengli1995.github.io/files/wsdm20.pdf) models pairwise time intervals alongside absolute positions, distinguishing irregularly spaced histories with identical item order. Its temporal mechanism is transferable inspiration, without replacing BERT4Rec’s backbone. [Parameter-Efficiently Leveraging Session Information (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109) explores lightweight session tokens, segment embeddings and temporal self-attention. [TSRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08531) models user-specific repeat intervals, item-specific timing and similarity to previous repeat sequences. Its repeat-consumption setting differs from unseen-item recommendation; repeated interactions alone do not establish continuing demand.\n\nA lightweight hypothesis for this task: retain one bidirectional BERT4Rec per category and add jointly learned attention-logit biases from bucketed log time gaps, optionally paired with per-head nonnegative temporal decay. This is a proposed adaptation, not a verified result from those papers. Different heads could learn different temporal sensitivities; compare interval-only and interval-plus-decay variants through macro validation HR@10. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690), appended-mask inference and final nonpadding readout. Compute temporal features only from available history; never supply the held-out interaction timestamp. If prediction time is unavailable, anchor appended-mask recency to the last observed event and acknowledge that this cannot measure elapsed time since that event. All temporal parameters should train jointly inside the single model."}
